result:
Life is like a river—relentless and gleaming, weaving through canyons and valleys, shaping rocks with nothing more than patience and time. It takes what it wants: smooth edges where there was once only jaggedness, deep pools where once there was dry sand.

Sometimes, I imagine it whispers to itself as it flows, *this is how things become beautiful*.

I don’t always listen as it should. I cling to the banks, worried about the next turn or the noise downstream. But the river doesn’t stop. It doesn’t apologize. It simply *is*, and in being, it exists abundantly—whether I wade in or not.

Yet, maybe willingness is part of the magic. When I let go, even partially, the water holds me. It doesn’t pull me under; it lifts. It carries. It cleans.

Sometimes I think we’re all just temporary vessels for something older—something that moves through us, shaping memory into meaning. We name it love. We call it art. We mistake it for luck or fate, when really it’s just the current doing what currents do.

And maybe that’s enough.
